result.title: Overcoming Prior Barriers: Supervised Fine-Tuning under Long-Tail Distribution
result.summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) adapts pretrained large language models (LLMs) to downstream tasks, but the required concepts can receive substantially different levels of pretrained support. Frequent concepts are more likely to be well learned, whereas rare concepts may remain weakly represented. We introduce a novel notion named prior barrier to quantify how strongly the pretrained model supports competing concepts over the target concept. We observe that prior barriers follow a long-tail distribution, placing head and tail concepts at different starting points for SFT: head concepts face lower prior barriers, whereas tail concepts require additional instructions to overcome their higher prior barriers. Our theoretical analysis further derives a predictive risk bound for SFT under long-tail prior barriers, explicitly characterizing how the prior barrier and accumulated SFT evidence jointly determine predictive performance. Motivated by this prior barrier-dependent demand, we propose PASS, an adaptive SFT instruction selection method that constructs reference-derived concepts and estimates the distinguishing evidence provided by each instruction, and adaptively allocates the selection budget toward concepts that remain insufficiently covered under the current selection. In this way, PASS jointly considers which instructions can provide useful evidence and where additional supervision is needed under a limited budget. Experiments show that our method consistently outperforms seven state-of-the-art instruction selection methods on four backbone-budget settings. An ablation study further shows that PASS's adaptive allocation consistently improves over uniform allocation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出用「prior barrier」量化预训练对目标概念相对竞争概念的支持强度，指出先验障碍呈长尾分布，并推导长尾障碍下 SFT 的预测风险上界，进而提出 PASS：按指令能提供的区分性证据，自适应地把有限选择预算分配到覆盖不足的概念上，在多个设置下优于七种指令选择方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按证据区分度 + 覆盖缺口分配预算」的指令选择思路，可能可供核查用于 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与监督/贡献分配的预算受限问题；但该工作为纯文本 SFT 数据选择，与推理期 latent 状态生成无直接关系。
